patchouli.zen_atelier.room_journal.landi: Rooms remember purpose. This journal keeps notes on anchors, comfort, craft, and the quiet habits that make a place useful.

Room types that can be recognized from anchors, furniture, and structure.
patchouli.zen_atelier.room_journal.entry: Rooms Remember Purpose
A room is more than walls. A bed, a lectern, a brewing stand, or a cauldron can give a place a clear purpose.
The room around that anchor matters too. Light, space, matching furniture, and a clear use make a room stronger.
Signals and Materials
Rooms read nearby blocks as signals. A signal is not always one exact block: a modded bookshelf can still feel like a bookshelf, and a different kind of workbench can still support a workshop.

The journal understands many common modded tags. Beds, bookshelves, crafting tables, furnaces, cauldrons, plants, glass, storage, and village work blocks can be recognized through shared tags when other mods provide them.

Industrial materials have their own scent. Concrete, chains, iron bars, lanterns, glasswork, machines, pipes, hoppers, pistons, and redstone machinery can make a room feel urban, factory-like, or simply too busy for quiet study.

Use that texture deliberately. Metal and stone help smithies and workshops, while factories belong away from bedrooms, gardens, libraries, and enchanting rooms unless you want the room to feel unsettled.
Anchors and Names
Anchors are the objects a room gathers around. A bed remembers rest. A brewing stand remembers work. A cauldron changes an ordinary workroom into an atelier.
The journal can inspect a room when used carefully on an anchor. It shows the room's name, type, score, and any special notes the room has earned.
Nameplates and Epithets
A sign placed near an anchor can become that room's nameplate. A blank sign adopts the current room name; a written sign gives the room a custom name.
Some rooms earn rare epithets when their purpose and details line up especially well. The practical room type remains underneath, but the discovered name is the one the room remembers.
Naming Rooms
A room can keep a custom name from a sign. Write the name you want, then place the sign beside the room it belongs to.
Use the sign with an empty hand while sneaking to apply its text. If the sign is waxed, an empty-hand use will also apply it. The name stays with the room when its shape is rechecked or saved.
Bedrooms
A bedroom begins with a bed, but comfort comes from the room around it. Light, space, storage, carpet, and a calm material palette all help.
A cramped or cluttered bedroom still counts as a bedroom. It simply may not be a very restful one.
Churches and Ateliers
A village church may keep a brewing stand for a cleric. It is useful, but it is not the same as a proper atelier.
An atelier needs both a brewing stand and a cauldron. Plants, pots, light, and careful furnishing make the room feel more complete.
Village Workrooms
Village work buildings are good places to study room purpose. A stonecutter suggests masonry, a loom suggests clothwork, and a lectern suggests a library.
The strongest rooms keep one clear job. Mixed rooms can still work, but the room may need better signs, storage, or furnishing to make its purpose obvious.
Smithies
A smithy is built around hot work and gear repair. An anvil, grindstone, smithing table, or blast furnace can all suggest the room's purpose.
Storage, stone, metal, and controlled heat make a smithy easier to read. Industrial materials help here when they serve the work instead of burying it.
Libraries
A library grows from bookshelves, chiseled bookshelves, and lecterns. It can stand alone or support an enchanting room.
Quiet rooms with clear walls, good light, and enough shelves make better libraries than a single lectern in a busy workshop.
Greenhouses
A greenhouse needs plants and enough glass to feel protected from the outside world.
Water, sunlight, glass, and plant variety all help the room feel like a place made for growing. Heavy machinery and urban materials pull that feeling away.
Terrariums
Some rooms are made for small wet lives. With Amphibia present, a terrarium is read as a planted, watered habitat rather than an ordinary greenhouse.
Frog-friendly plants, lily pads, dripleaves, damp corners, and shallow water help the room hold its identity. It should feel sheltered, alive, and easy to move through.
Keep machinery, heavy urban materials, and dry workshop clutter away. A terrarium wants humidity and cover, not factory noise.
Kitchens
A kitchen is a utility room for food, heat, and preparation. Smokers, furnaces, campfires, storage, and water access all help define it.
Kitchens can overlap with storage, but they make poor bedrooms. Heat and work clutter tend to make rest worse.
Storage Rooms
A storage room is strongest when containers are grouped with a clear purpose and enough space to reach them.
A few chests can support another room. Many chests can become the room's main identity.
Enchanting Rooms
An enchanting room centers on a table of magic, surrounded by the knowledge needed to understand it.
Bookshelves amplify enchantment power. A room with both a table and many books becomes a true place of magical study; factory clutter makes the room harder to read.
Masonry Shops
A mason works stone into shape. A stonecutter is the heart of a masonry shop, but storage and stone materials make it complete.
Masonry complements building, but too many other work types in the same room dilute its purpose.
Map Rooms
A map room is for careful planning and knowledge. A cartography table, reference books, and clear workspace define it.
Maps, charts, and planning tools help a room feel purposeful. Good lighting and quiet make it a better place to think.
Loom Rooms
A loom room is built for textile work. A loom is essential, but carpet, storage, and fine materials help too.
Textiles need space to work and display. A well-organized loom room shows care in every detail.
Fletcheries
A fletchery is for making and maintaining ranged equipment. A fletching table, storage, and tools define the craft.
Arrows, bows, and careful organization make a fletchery feel like a place of precision work.
Gardener's Sheds
A gardener's shed is a workspace for cultivating plants. A composter, pots, plants, and soil make it real.
Plant variety and careful gardening tools help define the room. It feels like a place where things grow.
Tanneries
A tannery is a workshop for working leather and materials through water. A cauldron is central to the craft.
Storage for hides and finished goods, water access, and working space define a proper tannery.
Churches
A church is a place of gathering and faith. It may have a brewing stand as part of its quiet hospitality.
Light, quiet, enclosure, and a sense of purpose make a room feel like a place of spiritual gathering.
Room Types & Hints
$(l)Room Hints$()$(br)Not sure what kind of room to build? Here are hints to guide your search. Rooms are listed from simplest to most complex.
$(l)The Fundamentals$()$(br)$(l)Bedroom:$() A place of rest. Every room starts with what it sleeps on.$(br)$(l)Storage:$() Things go in boxes. A room full of containers serves many purposes.
$(l)Kitchen:$() Heat and preparation. Food cooks where fires burn and supplies sit nearby.$(br)$(l)Library:$() Knowledge gathered on shelves. A room can be quiet and thoughtful.
$(l)Workshop:$() General purpose crafting. Where many trades can happen.$(br)$(l)Atelier:$() Alchemy and brewing. A cauldron with a brewing stand nearby.
$(l)Building Purpose$()$(br)$(l)Smithing:$() Hot work and repair. Where metal gets shaped and tools get fixed.$(br)$(l)Enchanting:$() Magic requires study. A table of power surrounded by knowledge.
$(l)Masonry:$() Stone takes shape. A workshop where stone and skill meet.$(br)$(l)Specialized Spaces$()$(br)$(l)Map Room:$() Planning and strategy. Charts, references, and careful layout.
$(l)Loom Room:$() Textiles need space. Woven materials and organized work.$(br)$(l)Fletchery:$() Precision and ranged work. The place where arrows and bows are made with care.

$(l)Complex Combinations$()$(br)$(l)Gardener's Shed:$() Plants need tending. Tools, compost, and careful cultivation.$(br)$(l)Greenhouse:$() Growth behind glass. Light, water, and protection together.

$(l)Tannery:$() Water and materials. A cauldron used alone, without brewing.$(br)$(l)The Sacred & Uncommon$()$(br)$(l)Church:$() Faith and gathering. A quiet place in a community, with simple comforts.
Common modded blocks can count when they use familiar tags. Once you find a room type, its full entry will unlock in this journal.
Room Discoveries

$(l)Progress Tracker$()$(br2)The next page lists every room profile the server knows about. Discovered rooms show their best score.$(br2)Undiscovered rooms keep their icon shadowed and offer clues for what to build next.

$(l)Using the Tracker$()$(br2)Explore and build to discover new rooms. Each room type has hints and requirements listed in this journal. Visit each room's full entry to understand its anchors, preferred materials, and design guidelines.
Room Stat Cards

$(l)Room Statistics$()$(br2)Each room type has a profile with its anchors, materials, and design requirements. Discovered rooms display their score - a measure of how well the space fulfills its purpose.

$(l)Understanding Scores$()$(br2)A score of 100 percent means the room has perfect anchors, matching materials, good light, adequate space, and no conflicting industrial elements. Lower scores still represent valid rooms - they simply serve their purpose less optimally.

patchouli.zen_atelier.room_journal.entry: How to Use This Journal

$(l)Room Discovery$()$(br2)This journal reads the spaces around you. Shift + right-click on a room's anchor (bed, brewing stand, furnace, etc.) to inspect it. The journal reveals what type of room it recognizes and how well the space serves that purpose.

$(l)The Score$()$(br2)Each discovered room earns a score from 0-100% based on its design. A complete room has the right anchor, matching furniture, good lighting, adequate space, and materials that reinforce its purpose. Poor rooms are still valid; they simply serve their function less well.

$(l)Custom Names$()$(br2)Write a name on a sign, then place it next to a room's anchor while holding the sign. Sneak + right-click the sign with an empty hand to apply the name. That room will remember its custom name and use it in the journal.

$(l)Progress Tracking$()$(br2)Visit the 'Room Discoveries' entry to see all room profiles the server recognizes. Discovered rooms show their best score. Undiscovered rooms offer hints to guide your building. The journal remembers what you've found.
Ateliers

An atelier needs both a brewing stand and a cauldron. The distinction from a church lies in the pairing: a brewing stand alone can serve a cleric, but with a cauldron it becomes a true workspace for potion craft.
Plants, pots, light, and careful furnishing make the room feel more complete. Storage for ingredients, organized work surfaces, and space to gather materials help the craft flourish.
$(room)Anchors:$() Brewing Stand + Cauldron. $(signal)Materials:$() Plant blocks, cauldrons, potion bottles, storage. $(warn)Avoid:$() Heavy machinery and factories clash with quiet alchemy work.
Farm Pens

A farm pen is a contained space for raising animals or tending crops. Hay bales, fences, feeders, and water access define the space. The room must feel intentional - a place made for living things to thrive.
Plant variety, water features, clear fencing, and organized feeding areas help the room feel purposeful. Heavy machinery and industrial materials make the space feel hostile to animal life.
$(room)Anchors:$() Bee Hive, Composter, or Nesting Box. $(signal)Materials:$() Hay, fences, water, compost. $(warn)Avoid:$() Concrete, machines, heavy industrial blocks.
$(room)Anchors:$() Brewing Stand (alone). $(signal)Materials:$() Candles, bells, quiet blocks, calm colors. $(warn)Avoid:$() Loud machinery and industrial clutter.
$(room)Anchors:$() Bed. $(signal)Materials:$() Carpet, calm colors, warm light, decorative storage. $(warn)Avoid:$() Furnaces, cauldrons, and work clutter.
$(room)Anchors:$() Containers (chests, barrels, bundles). $(signal)Materials:$() Organized storage blocks, shelving, space. $(warn)Avoid:$() Mixing storage with active work stations.
$(room)Anchors:$() Farmland or Potted Azalea. $(signal)Materials:$() Glass, plants, water, light. $(warn)Avoid:$() Dark corners and industrial machinery.
$(room)Anchors:$() Enchanting Table. $(signal)Materials:$() Bookshelves, candles, dark oak, amethyst. $(warn)Avoid:$() Factory noise and urban clutter.
$(room)Anchors:$() Lectern or Chiseled Bookshelf. $(signal)Materials:$() Bookshelves, quiet blocks, tables for study. $(warn)Avoid:$() Loud work stations and machines.
$(room)Anchors:$() Furnace, Smoker, or Campfire. $(signal)Materials:$() Storage, water, heat sources, organized prep space. $(warn)Avoid:$() Pure decoration without function.
$(room)Anchors:$() Anvil, Grindstone, or Smithing Table. $(signal)Materials:$() Stone, metal, heat sources, tool storage. $(warn)Avoid:$() Cluttered layouts that hide the work.
$(room)Anchors:$() Loom. $(signal)Materials:$() Wool, carpet, dyes, organized textile storage. $(warn)Avoid:$() Competing work stations in the same space.
$(room)Anchors:$() Fletching Table. $(signal)Materials:$() Arrows, wood, feathers, organized equipment storage. $(warn)Avoid:$() Mixing fletching with unrelated crafts.
$(room)Anchors:$() Cartography Table. $(signal)Materials:$() Maps, charts, tables, quiet workspace. $(warn)Avoid:$() Loud machinery that disrupts concentration.
$(room)Anchors:$() Composter or Composters. $(signal)Materials:$() Plants, pots, soil blocks, water. $(warn)Avoid:$() Urban materials that feel out of place.
$(room)Anchors:$() Stonecutter. $(signal)Materials:$() Stone variants, chisel blocks, storage for materials. $(warn)Avoid:$() Competing crafts that dilute purpose.
$(room)Anchors:$() Cauldron (alone, no brewing stand). $(signal)Materials:$() Water access, hides, drying racks, storage. $(warn)Avoid:$() Mixing with potion work or other crafts.
$(room)Anchors:$() Farmland with frog-friendly plants (with Amphibia mod). $(signal)Materials:$() Lily pads, dripleaves, damp blocks, water. $(warn)Avoid:$() Dry machinery and industrial noise.
Visual Room Reference

$(l)Room Type Quick Reference$()$(br2)Each room type has a unique combination of anchors (core blocks), signals (supportive blocks), and warnings (blocks to avoid).$(br2)Use this guide to quickly identify what makes each room special.

$(l)Core Room Types$()$(br)$(room)Bedroom:$() Sleep | Lamp, Calm, Storage$(br)$(room)Kitchen:$() Heat | Pot, Water, Food$(br)$(room)Storage:$() Organization | Containers, Access$(br)$(room)Library:$() Knowledge | Books, Quiet, Space$(br)$(room)Atelier:$() Craft | Brewing + Cauldron + Plants

$(l)Specialized Workrooms$()$(br)$(room)Smithy:$() Hammer | Heat, Stone, Metal$(br)$(room)Enchanting:$() Magic | Table, Books, Power$(br)$(room)Workshop:$() Tools | Versatile, Organized$(br)$(room)Masonry:$() Stone | Stonecutter, Focus$(br)$(room)Loom:$() Threads | Weaving, Care

$(l)Nature & Production$()$(br)$(room)Greenhouse:$() Plants | Glass, Light, Water$(br)$(room)Farm Pen:$() Animals | Space, Fences, Water$(br)$(room)Gardener's Shed:$() Growth | Tools, Plants, Soil$(br)$(room)Tannery:$() Leather | Cauldron, Water, Hides

$(l)Specialized Crafts$()$(br)$(room)Fletchery:$() Arrows | Table, Precision$(br)$(room)Map Room:$() Charts | Cartography, Light$(br)$(room)Church:$() Faith | Quiet, Gathering$(br)$(room)Terrarium:$() Wet Life | Plants, Water, Shelter

$(l)Design Principle$()$(br2)Strong rooms keep their purpose clear and unmixed. A smithy full of enchanting tables is hard to read. A bedroom full of furnaces prevents rest.$(br2)Supporting materials reinforce purpose: stone and metal help smithies, calm colors help bedrooms, glass helps greenhouses.$(br2)Industrial machinery clashes with peaceful spaces and crafting rooms. Use it deliberately or keep it separate.
Room Stat Cards

$(l)Room Stat Cards$()$(br2)Below you'll see a sample stat card showing a room's details. $(room)Discovered rooms$() display their score, tier, and rating in an easy-to-scan format. $(warn)Undiscovered rooms$() show hints and a silhouette to guide your discovery.

$(l)Card Information$()$(br)$(room)Score:$() 0-100% based on room design and quality$(br)$(room)Tier:$() Poor, Fair, Good, Excellent (based on score)$(br)$(room)Stars:$() Visual rating from ☆ to ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐$(br)$(br)$(warn)Hints$() help you identify what to build. Different room types have different anchor blocks and supporting materials.
